title: POC deployment pathways workshop notes — Acme Finance
content:
Objective:
Run a 6-week technical POC for Acme Finance to validate three deployment pathways (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and recommend a production deployment option. Focus areas: latency SLO, data residency/compliance, model customization, cost per 1k tokens, and operational runbook needs.

Customer context (summary):
- Org: Acme Finance (regulated payments platform).
- Key constraints: PCI-adjacent data, EU and US data residency, strict audit trails, SOC2+ and upcoming regional regulator audit.
- Traffic profile for POC: 60 qps peak across 2 regions (US-EAST + EU-WEST) for short-chat prompts (avg 80 tokens request + 120 tokens response).
- Desired SLOs: 95th perc latency < 200ms for short requests; cold-start under 2s; throughput sustained at 120 qps per region during load tests.
- Budget target: unit inference cost <$0.08 per 1k tokens for steady-state workload.

Design options evaluated (high level):
1) Hosted (Redwood API, multi-tenant control plane + Redwood compute):
   - Pros: fastest setup, minimal onboarding (API key), streaming support out-of-the-box, Redwood handles kernel & batch tuning, lower initial ops burden.
   - Cons: multitenancy implies limited control over host-level network controls; data residency possible via region selection but not full private control plane; some customers require private control plane for audit logs.
   - Fit for Acme? Quick demo and can validate latency and correctness; may not meet compliance needs for regulated production.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity — customer-dedicated GPU pool in Redwood-managed infra):
   - Pros: dedicated GPUs for predictable latency/throughput, isolated tenant compute, stronger contract terms (SLA), can enable custom quantization and model variants. Good middle ground.
   - Cons: higher cost than hosted; provisioning lead time (hours to days depending on capacity); still uses Redwood control plane (but can be configured for tighter audit logging and egress restrictions).
   - Fit for Acme? Likely viable for early production if control plane audit/contractual needs satisfied and regional placement possible.

3) Private (VPC or on-prem private deployment):
   - Pros: full network isolation, KMS/HSM integration, data never leaves customer environment, highest compliance suitability. Can run on-prem or in customer VPC cloud.
   - Cons: longest onboarding, customer infra ops responsibility, need for on-site GPU capacity planning and SRE handoff; potential feature lag vs hosted.
   - Fit for Acme? Required for regulated production if legal insists on private control plane or air-gapped environment.

Hybrid and fallbacks considered:
- Control-plane hybrid: Redwood control plane in customer's VPC (managed private control plane) + compute in customer VPC or dedicated Redwood nodes. Gives balance between features and isolation.
- Multi-tier routing: primary -> dedicated (low-cost) or private (for regulated flows) with automatic fallback to hosted for non-sensitive requests if remaining healthy.

Technical design variants (not exhaustive):
- Model variants: base open model (e.g., Llama2-derived) quantized int8 for cost; dedicated can run fp16 for latency-sensitive paths.
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix caching in Dedicated to reduce token costs for repetitive customer prompts (expected 18-25% token savings).
- Batching policy: continuous batching on Dedicated to improve GPU efficiency while keeping per-request latency under SLO via adaptive max-batch-size throttles.
- Endpoint routing: use request attributes (customer_id, data_sensitivity flag) to route to Private/Dedicated/Hosted via Redwood smart-routing policies.

POC plan (6 weeks) — milestone summary:
- Week 0 (prep): finalize scope & legal checklist, access tokens, region selection, sample traffic generator.
- Week 1: Hosted quickstart demo (baseline latency, correctness), collect baseline metrics.
- Week 2-3: Provision Dedicated pool (2x A10 equivalent nodes per region), deploy model variants, run integration tests.
- Week 4: Private trial in customer VPC (small instance), validate network, KMS integration, audit log delivery.
- Week 5: Load testing and chaos tests (node failure, region failover), latency/cost measurements.
- Week 6: Evaluation, decision workshop, handoff materials + runbook.

Success criteria (for decision):
- Functional: model responses meet acceptance prompts (no hallucinations on X% of tests; accuracy/precision thresholds defined in evaluation doc).
- Performance: 95th perc latency < 200ms for target workload in chosen deployment; cold-start <2s for node scale events.
- Reliability: automated failover across zones without >1% increased error rate during failover tests.
- Security/Compliance: audit logs delivered to customer SIEM and KMS symmetric key rotation validated.
- Cost: steady-state token cost <= target budget (per POC traffic profile).

Test matrix (samples):
- Functional correctness: 2000 prompt set from Acme's domain (payments phrases), run across model variants, compare rouge/bleu/acceptance labels.
- Latency tests: ramp 0->120 qps in 10 mins per region, measure p50/p95/p99.
- Failover: kill a node, observe request routing and cold-start times.
- Security: verify VPC endpoints, mTLS between Redwood control plane and compute, validate KMS keys.

Workshop notes / decisions made during session: 
- Agreed to run Hosted baseline first for quick ROI visibility. (Decision owner: Asha Patel)
- Acme legal requires audit logs to be forwarded to their Splunk instance for all production workloads. For the POC, they will accept log forwarding from Dedicated nodes. (Owner: Jae Kim)
- Network egress must remain inside EU for EU customers; we will validate region pinning on Dedicated. (Owner: Miguel Ortega)
- Customer prefers model customization; discuss custom fine-tuning cadence and data residency with research team. (Action: Samir Rao to scope fine-tune pipeline)

Open questions / risks:
- Regulatory: does the upcoming regional regulator require air-gapped operations for payment intent data? If yes, Private becomes mandatory. (Legal to confirm by 2024-10-09)
- Sizing: initial Dedicated sizing estimate is conservative — need real telemetry after Hosted baseline to finalize node counts.
- SLA expectations: Acme asked for 99.9% for production; need to map to Dedicated contract tiers.

Action items (owner / due):
- Asha Patel: run Hosted baseline + share p95/p99 metrics (due 2024-09-25) — JIRA: POC-412.
- Miguel Ortega: provision Dedicated pool in us-east1 and eu-west1 (estimate 2 nodes/region) and post cost estimate (due 2024-09-29).
- Samir Rao: draft fine-tune data pipeline options and privacy-preserving tuning notes (due 2024-10-03).
- Jae Kim: get legal confirmation on audit-forwarding requirements and whether customer will accept Dedicated for POC (due 2024-10-09).

Operational runbook highlights (POC scope):
- Oncall rotation: solutions-eng will provide 24/7 SLA coverage during final two weeks of load testing.
- Escalation path: Slack #poc-acme -> eng-sre -> product-hosted-api lead.
- Rollback strategy: traffic split 90/10 -> 50/50 -> 0/100 with automated rollback on error rate >2% or latency breach for >5 minutes.

Sample routing policy (pseudo-config):
- if request.data_sensitivity == \"high\" and region == "eu-west1" then route -> private-vpc-eu
- else if customer_tier == \"enterprise\" then route -> dedicated-pool
- else route -> hosted-default

Documentation to produce for handoff:
- Final architecture decision memo (Confluence).
- POC metrics dump (CSV + Grafana dashboards).
- Runbook: failover, incident response, scale-up procedures.

Appendix / references: 
- Linked JIRA: POC-412 (POC plan and tasks)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/poc-acme-deploy/pull/7 (deployment manifests and sample scripts)
- Confluence: Acme Finance POC overview (design diagrams and evaluation rubric)

Meeting wrap / next steps:
- Team will implement Hosted baseline (Asha) and report metrics next Wed.
- Dedicated pool cost estimate and provisioning timeline from infra (Miguel) due end of week.
- Legal to confirm compliance constraints; if air-gap required, reprioritize Private onboarding in sprint.

Notes to self: keep configs parameterized for region pinning and KMS aliases; preserve test IDs in logs for easy traceability (use header X-POC-ID).

End of document.
